sections.html:
In Jackson County, a tax bill passes through three desks in McKee. Someone values your land, someone takes your payment, and someone files your deed.

Jackson County tax offices, all with P.O. boxes in McKee, KY
OfficeMailing address and phoneRole
PVAP.O. Box 249, 40447; (606) 287-7634; fax (606) 287-7079Keeps property records and assesses property
SheriffP.O. Box 426, 40447; (606) 287-7121Collects taxes
County ClerkP.O. Box 339, 40447; (606) 287-7800Files deeds, mortgages and transfers

Call the Sheriff to find out which payment methods and counter hours apply. The offices sit close together in McKee, so a seller can usually settle the bill, ask a PVA question and drop off a deed in a single trip if the phone calls come first.

No local calendar overrides the state one. The bill is due by December 31 under KRS 134.015, and a 2 percent discount goes to anyone who pays the whole thing by November 1.

Paid by November 1, the bill is 2 percent lighter. Through the rest of December the printed figure is what you owe. In January a 5 percent penalty arrives, and from February onward it is 10 percent.

If bills go out late, Revenue can set a stretched schedule with a month per stage. The Sheriff stops collecting on April 15, and the Clerk holds whatever is left. Didn't get a bill? Phone the Sheriff anyway. A lost bill won't cancel a penalty.

Begin with the PVA. KRS 133.120 requires a conference first, held before or during the inspection period. Can't get to the office? Ask for a phone call.

Still unhappy afterward? Put your reasons in a written petition, identify the parcel, say what you believe fair cash value is, and deliver or mail it to the County Clerk. Get it to the Clerk by the first workday after inspection wraps up. The bill itself arrives too late to contest, so watch for the inspection notice instead.

The board of assessment appeals then holds a public hearing. Before it meets, pull together whatever proves your number:

  • A description of the land and buildings.
  • Insurance policies and construction costs.
  • Listings, contracts or a recent appraisal.
  • Loan or mortgage papers on the parcel.

Rural parcels are hard to compare, so a recent appraisal or a sale of a similar tract nearby carries more weight than a general complaint. Without evidence, the petition may simply be denied. While the case runs, keep paying tax on the value you claimed.

An eligible owner takes $49,100 off the assessed value in 2025 and 2026. With a middle home value of $111,500 in this county, that takes out a big slice of the taxable base.

Two tests apply: it must be your own home, and you must be 65 or older, or totally disabled by a federal or retirement-system standard. Age is proven with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport brought to the PVA. Disabled owners reapply annually, unless the disability is service-connected or Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled it permanent.

The break belongs to the home where you live now. Once you sell and move, notify the PVA and apply at the new address.

Budget to clear it from the money you receive at the sale. The tax is a personal debt that dates from the assessment date. A lien on the land can last 11 years. On April 15, an open bill becomes a certificate of delinquency at the Clerk.

From there the schedule moves quickly. A County Attorney notice goes out within 30 days of transfer, and a second one within 60 if needed. Under KRS 134.128 the tax sale follows 90 to 135 days after transfer, with the Clerk advertising the list 30 to 45 days beforehand. Commissions and interest accumulate in that window, so call the Jackson County Clerk at (606) 287-7800 for an actual payoff.

Request the figure in writing, ideally before the listing agreement is signed. The title company can then send the Clerk a check from your proceeds. Selling to a cash buyer changes nothing here, since the debt stays with the land until it is paid.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and transfer tax
sections.html:
The County Clerk's McKee office records your deed. That office also issues vehicle and marriage licenses, keeps wills and notary bonds, and collects the state transfer tax before it accepts a deed.

Under KRS 142.050 the seller, as grantor, owes 50 cents on each $500 of value. A few transfers owe nothing, including gifts of nominal value, transfers between divorcing spouses and foreclosures.

Recording fees come from statute and can change, so get today's amount from the Clerk ahead of closing.

sections.h2: Jackson County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Jackson County has 13,325 residents, up 2.8 percent since 2020. About 77.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The middle home value is $111,500, median gross rent is $665 and median household income is $40,000. A typical commute runs 37.7 minutes.

Monthly owner costs average $1,101 with a mortgage and $355 without. Most residents stay: 91.9 percent lived at the same address a year earlier. Nearly every sale is of an existing house, and its assessment goes back to the PVA's value on January 1.

McKee is the county seat and Annville is the largest community. Three industrial parks, in Annville, McKee and Sandgap, anchor local jobs.

sections.h2: What to bring to the offices
sections.html:
Pull out your newest tax bill and your deed before listing. If you are contesting a value, add photos, an appraisal or comparable sales. For the homestead exemption, bring proof of age. Mail is slow in a rural county, so call first and ask whether the office wants originals or copies. Ask too whether the Sheriff takes cards or only checks and cash.

At closing, the title company usually makes the recording trip. Confirm with the Clerk that the transfer tax and recording fee will be collected at filing, and keep the receipt for your records.

sections.h2: If you want to sell fast
sections.html:
A quick sale works best when the paperwork is ready. Find out which office holds your bill today: the Sheriff before April 15, the Clerk after. Get a written payoff, check that the deed is in your name, and confirm whether a homestead exemption is on the account. A buyer paying cash can close in days, but the tax payoff and the deed recording still have to happen first.

If you are behind on several years, ask the Clerk whether any certificate has been sold, because a buyer's added charges raise the payoff.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Jackson County PVA?
faqs.a: Send mail to P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447. The phone is (606) 287-7634 and the fax line is (606) 287-7079.

faqs.q: What is the discount for paying early?
faqs.a: The discount is 2 percent, and it requires paying the full bill by November 1 under KRS 134.015. From then until year end you owe the printed amount.

faqs.q: What does a late payment cost?
faqs.a: A 5 percent penalty applies in January, then 10 percent. A bill still open on April 15 goes to the Clerk, where 1 percent monthly interest and commissions begin.

faqs.q: Can a seller keep the homestead exemption after leaving?
faqs.a: No. It covers only your current residence. After closing, tell the PVA and apply again for your new residence.

faqs.q: Is the deed recorded at the McKee courthouse?
faqs.a: Yes. The County Clerk handles it and collects the transfer tax, 50 cents per $500. Call (606) 287-7800 to confirm current fees.
